title: Start with a forecast
outcome: Build a reproducible match table and a baseline: a simple reference prediction.

blocks.body: Question: Can a simple rule predict a match?
Mathematics: Refresh fractions, ratios, percentages, means, variables, functions, and summation through match statistics.

Dataset: StatsBomb Open Data: competitions.json → matches/{competition_id}/{season_id}.json. Use scores, dates, and information available before kickoff. Build recent-form features only from earlier matches.
Reading: ISL chapter 2. Use a small competition first. Preserve the same held-out test period throughout the project.

blocks.title: StatsBomb Open Data
blocks.note: Use the README, competition list, match files, event schema, and attribution terms. Select a historical competition with enough matches.

blocks.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning · Python
blocks.note: Use selected chapters and Python labs. The book PDF is free on the authors’ site.

blocks.body: Challenge: Recompute a three-outcome Brier score for one match. Explain why all three probabilities must sum to one.

tasks.prompt: Load historical matches. Record the source, download date, license, and a small data dictionary.
